chunks: Al-Shahid al-Thani said, having written in some of his notes in his own handwriting:

The Master, the Imam, the Blessed, the Most Learned, the Most Excellent, the Most God-fearing, the Most Scrupulous — Abu Abdallah Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn al-Nu'man al-Mufid — may Allah sanctify his soul and purify his grave.

key_terms.الشَّهِيدُ الثَّانِي: al-Shahid al-Thani (the Second Martyr), Zayn al-Din al-Juba'i al-Amili (d. 966 AH)
key_terms.الْأَوْرَعُ: the most scrupulous in piety and abstinence (wara')
key_terms.رَمْسَهُ: his grave, burial place (classical term for the covered tomb)

ai.seo_question: What titles did al-Shahid al-Thani write in his handwritten notes to praise Sheikh al-Mufid?
ai.summary: Al-Shahid al-Thani records in his own handwriting in some of his notes a eulogy of Sheikh al-Mufid (Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn al-Nu'man, d. 413 AH), honouring him with the loftiest titles: the Master, the Imam, the Blessed, the Most Learned, the Most Excellent, the Most God-fearing, and the Most Scrupulous in piety. He closes with the invocation: 'May Allah sanctify his soul and purify his grave.' This entry appears in the chapter of Tahdhib al-Ahkam dedicated to praises of al-Mufid, reflecting the reverence later Shia scholars bore for him.
